{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ce1b0ad5259e264f3ffb1604bd60d8f3cd81963795642b642cfb6b27bf58ff91","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:49","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road — C2.01","heading":"C2 — Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Crashes, vehicle equipment and sharing the road
FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
The slow-moving-vehicle symbol warns that the vehicle ahead cannot travel faster than 25 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
Slow-moving vehicles have a legal right to use the roadway, so respond patiently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Tractor-trailers behave differently from passenger cars when accelerating, braking, climbing, changing lanes or turning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
The fuller Move Over passage covers an emergency or authorized municipal, public-utility, construction or maintenance vehicle stopped or moving under 20 mph on or within three feet of the roadway with warning lights or signals active. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A01
The Move Over passage requires the applicable response as soon as it is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A01
For that provision on an interstate or other highway with at least two lanes in the warning vehicle's direction, merge to the farthest lane or leave at least one traffic lane of separation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A02
Police directions override the Move Over lane-separation instruction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A02
The later Move Over passage directs a driver on a two-lane road posted at 45 mph or above to travel 20 mph below the posted limit unless police direct otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A02
Wildlife collisions on rural Wyoming roads can injure or kill vehicle occupants as well as animals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A02
Animal collisions can happen year-round but are most common during spring and fall migrations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A02
Slow down and use extra caution where deer-crossing signs appear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A02
When watching for animals, scan the road ahead and both roadsides. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A02
At night, use high beams when possible to illuminate the road and roadside while watching for animals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A02
Be especially watchful for animals near forested areas and water. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A03
Be particularly alert for animals at dawn and dusk, when feeding activity and reduced visibility coincide. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A03
Watch for headlight reflections in animals' eyes ahead. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A03
When an animal is on or near the road, slow down, tap the brakes to warn following drivers and sound the horn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A03
Harder braking for an animal is possible when no vehicle is following behind. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A03
Flashing headlights at an animal can cause it to freeze in the roadway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A03
If an animal collision seems unavoidable, do not swerve suddenly; brake as quickly as safely possible while keeping control and staying on the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A03
Report an animal collision to local law enforcement, especially when the animal's body remains a hazard on the highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0073]
